citation: Treaty with the Ottawa, etc., 1816 (St. Louis, 24 August 1816; 7 Stat. 146), in Charles J. Kappler, ed., Indian Affairs: Laws and Treaties, vol. II, Treaties (Washington: Government Printing Office, 1904).
author: the United States commissioners Ninian Edwards, William Clark and Auguste Chouteau, and the chiefs and warriors of the united Ottawa, Chippewa and Potawatomi of the Illinois and Milwaukee rivers; compiled by Charles J. Kappler
repository: Oklahoma State University Libraries, Tribal Treaties Database (Kappler vol. II transcription)
locator: the preamble ('the chiefs and warriors of the united tribes of Ottawas, Chipawas, and Pottowotomees, residing on the Illinois and Melwakee rivers'); Article 1, the cession of the strip about Chicago; the signatures, among them Mucketeypokee, Mucketepennese, Wapunsy, Chamblee, 'Richeikeming, or Lake', 'Pemasaw, or Walker', 'Nangesay, alias Stout', 'Tawwaning, or Trader', 'Mowais, or Little Wolf', and Sinnowchewone 'by his brother Ignatius'.
rights_note: A United States treaty and a 1904 Government Printing Office compilation; public domain. Read as the OSU transcription.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-08 for T-3508 from the OSU page (fetched that day), checked against the Department's 1837 Indian Treaties (Internet Archive indiantreatiesa00deptgoog) for the spellings.
note: THE CESSION OF THE LAND ABOUT CHICAGO. Its signers are the chiefs and warriors of the bands of the Chicago country four years after the attack on the column; several are named in the sources of 1812 (Black Partridge, the Blackbird, Waubansee). The treaty does not say who was at Chicago in 1812.
what_it_supplies: the names of the chiefs and warriors of the united bands of the Illinois and Milwaukee rivers in 1816, several with English glosses
what_it_does_not_supply: where any signer was in August 1812
